# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

The previous call was rejected because `-.` is not a legal gesture symbol. I can communicate directly with the Mute using speech, so I’m sending the complete visual information plainly and asking the Mute to relay the applicable manual instructions to the Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb visual state: display 8. Light green. Wires in order: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Read the manual and tell the Blind exactly what action to perform.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👌 👍]

I cannot interpret the Mute’s four gestures because no gesture code was established, and gestures cannot reach the Blind. I will explicitly direct the Mute to use speech, which the Blind can hear, and to relay the manual’s exact action for the displayed bomb state.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your gestures are not readable by the Blind. Speak the exact manual instruction aloud for the Blind: display 8, green light, wires red yellow blue. Do not use gestures.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

I still do not have the manual, so I cannot determine which wire or action is safe from the visual facts alone. The Mute’s gesture is not an established code and cannot substitute for the manual’s spoken instruction. I am asking the Mute once more to state the exact procedure aloud so the Blind can act.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Speak the manual procedure aloud to Blind now. State exactly what the Blind must do for display 8, green light, and wires red, yellow, blue. Do not gesture.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

I now recognize the Mute’s code: 👍 is a Morse dot, 👎 is a dash, 👌 separates letters, and ✊ separates words. The long first message begins with “BLUE GREEN,” confirming the code. Since the remaining manual text is not yet safely decoded, I’m asking the Mute to send only the decisive action in Morse. I will tell the Blind to wait rather than risk an unsupported action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use Morse gestures: thumbs up dot, thumbs down dash, OK separates letters, fist separates words. Send only the exact safe action for this bomb, preferably the wire number and any required operation.")
speak(to="blind", text="Wait. The Mute is encoding the manual instruction in gestures for me; I will relay the exact action.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 👎 👍 👌 👍 👍 👎 👌 👎 👌 👍 👍 👍 👌 ✊ 👌 👎 👎 👎 👎 👍 👌 ✊ 👎 👎 👎 👎 👍 👌 👎 👍 👍 👎 👌 👍 👌 👎 👎 👎 👎 👎]

The latest Morse decodes as `CUTS 9X E0`, which is not a sufficiently clear or valid instruction for the Blind. I will not convert an ambiguous signal into a bomb action. I’m asking the Mute to state the safe wire and operation unambiguously in speech, which the Blind can hear.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your Morse message is ambiguous: CUTS 9X E0. Speak clearly to Blind: specify wire 1, 2, or 3, and whether to cut, leave, or perform another operation.")
speak(to="blind", text="Do not act yet. The instruction received so far is ambiguous; wait for the Mute to state the exact wire and operation aloud.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👎 👌 👎 👍 👌 👍 👌 ✊ 👍 👎 👎 👌 👎 👍 👎 👍 👌 👍 ✊ 👎 👍 👍 👎 👌 👎]

The established Morse decoding of the latest gesture string is `ONE WCE X`, which is not a valid instruction. I will not guess a wire or operation. The Blind should continue waiting while the Mute gives a clear spoken instruction or a corrected Morse message.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Do not act. The latest decoded message is invalid: ONE WCE X. Wait for a clear manual instruction.")
speak(to="mute", text="Latest Morse decodes as ONE WCE X, which is invalid. Please speak the exact instruction aloud to Blind, or resend corrected Morse with thumbs up dot, thumbs down dash, OK between letters, and fist between words.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👎 👌 👍 👍 👌 👍 👎 👍 👌 👍 👌 👌 👎 👎 👎 👌 👎 👍 👌 👍 👌 ✊ 👎 👍 👎 👍 👌 👍 👍 👎 👌 👎 👍]

The Morse decodes to `WIRE ONE CUN`; the first word is clearly `WIRE`, but the final word is malformed and is not safely interpretable as `CUT`. I will not guess the operation. I’m asking the Mute to correct it in speech for the Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your Morse decodes to WIRE ONE CUN, not a valid operation. Speak the exact instruction to Blind, including whether to cut wire 1.")
speak(to="blind", text="Do not act yet. The decoded message is malformed: WIRE ONE CUN. Wait for the Mute to clarify the operation aloud.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 👎 👍 👌 👍 👍 👎 👌 👎 ✊ 👍 👎 👎 👌 👍 👍 👌 👍 👎 👍 👌 👍 ✊ 👎 👎 👎 👌 👎 👍 👌 👍]

The Mute’s Morse message decodes unambiguously as “CUT WIRE ONE.” The visual state is display 8, green light, with wire 1 red. I am relaying that exact action to the Blind, who can perform it.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The manual instruction is: cut wire one. Cut the red wire, wire 1.")
```
